## 1. `packs/science/content/b2/b2-blood-and-vessels/bundle.json`

### B1 [major] `q…0008` part `main` (3 marks): three spellings of the swap still score 3/3, and the one that is caught now loses the backflow mark too

Current (identical `reject` copied onto all three groups):

```json
"keyWords": [
  {"any":["low pressure","lower pressure","little pressure"],"marks":1,
   "reject":["artery is at low pressure","arteries are at low pressure","artery at low pressure",
             "vein is at high pressure","veins are at high pressure","vein at high pressure",
             "arteries have valves"]},
  {"any":["backwards","back flow","backflow","wrong direction"],"marks":1,"reject":[ …same… ]},
  {"any":["high pressure","higher pressure"],"marks":1,"reject":[ …same… ]}
]
```

Probe, current content:

| response | marks |
|---|---|
| "Veins carry blood at **high** pressure, so valves stop backflow. Arteries carry blood at **low** pressure." | **3/3** |
| "A vein **has high pressure** and an artery **has low pressure**, so the vein needs valves to stop backward flow." | **3/3** |
| "Blood in a vein is at high pressure, so the valves stop it flowing backwards. Blood in an artery is at low pressure." | **0/3** — the backflow mark, which is correct, is cancelled with the rest |

The groups are presence-based and the words "low pressure" and "high pressure" carry no vessel, so
any swap that avoids the seven enumerated spellings scores everything.

**Fix** — key groups 1 and 3 to the vessel and delete all three `reject` lists:

```json
"keyWords": [
  {"any":["vein is at low pressure","veins are at low pressure","vein at low pressure","veins at low pressure",
          "blood in a vein is at low","blood in veins is at low","low pressure in a vein","low pressure in the vein",
          "low pressure in veins","veins carry blood at low pressure","vein carries blood at low pressure",
          "vein has low pressure","veins have low pressure","pressure in a vein is low","pressure in the vein is low",
          "pressure in veins is low"],"marks":1},
  {"any":["backwards","back flow","backflow","wrong direction"],"marks":1},
  {"any":["artery is at high pressure","arteries are at high pressure","artery at high pressure","arteries at high pressure",
          "blood in an artery is at high","blood in arteries is at high","high pressure in an artery","high pressure in the artery",
          "high pressure in arteries","arteries carry blood at high pressure","artery carries blood at high pressure",
          "artery has high pressure","arteries have high pressure","pressure in an artery is high",
          "pressure in the artery is high"],"marks":1}
]
```

Re-run: `accepted` 3/3, `workedSolution` 3/3, three correct paraphrases 3/3 each (including the
plural and "the pressure in a vein is low" forms), and all four swap wordings **1/3** — the backflow
mark, which is genuinely earned, survives and the two pressure marks do not.

### B2 [major] `q…0009` part `main` (3 marks): the new reject list zeroes two correct answers, and the reversed answer still scores 2/3

Current (identical `reject` on all three groups):

```json
"reject":["water leaves the cells","water leaves them","water moves out","out of the cells",
          "water is lost from the cells"]
```

Probe, current content:

| response | marks |
|---|---|
| "Water enters by osmosis because the water outside is more dilute. The cells swell and burst, because there is no cell wall to keep the water **out of the cells**." | **0/3** — fully correct |
| "Water enters the cells by osmosis and they burst, because they have no cell wall. In a concentrated salt solution **water leaves the cells** instead and they shrink." | **0/3** — fully correct, and it is the contrast the item's own figure teaches ("in concentrated salt / water leaves, so the cell / shrinks and crinkles") |
| "Water **passes out** by osmosis and the cells shrivel, because they have no cell wall." | **2/3** — reversed direction |
| "The water **goes from the cells** into the distilled water by osmosis, so they shrink; they have no cell wall." | **2/3** — reversed direction |

The reject fires on the phrase wherever it occurs, including in a correct clause, and the reversal
itself is still scored by group 2's unqualified `"osmosis"`.

**Fix** — key group 2 to water *entering* and delete all three `reject` lists:

```json
{"any":["water enters","water moves in","water moves into","water passes in","water goes in",
        "water is taken in","water flows in","enters by osmosis","enters the cells",
        "into the cells by osmosis","takes in water","take in water"],"marks":1}
```

Re-run: `accepted`, `workedSolution` and all three correct answers above 3/3; the three reversed
answers **1/3** (the "no cell wall" mark only). A residual worth noting: a reversed answer still
keeps that one mark, because "they have no cell wall" is a true statement in isolation; CCEA would
give 0. Tightening group 3 to `"no cell wall to limit"` / `"no cell wall so they burst"` would close
it, at the cost of rejecting the bare-but-creditable "they have no cell wall" — the reviewer's call.

### B3 [major] `q…0001` parts `a` and `b` (1 mark each): `listingRule: true` zeroes the specification's own wording

Both parts carry `"listingRule": true` with a single key-word group. `countListedItems` treats any
answer whose comma/and-separated segments are all four words or fewer as a list, so a two-clause
answer counts as two items against one group and loses the mark.

| part | response | marks |
|---|---|---|
| (a) "State the function of the white blood cells." | "they fight disease and infection" | **0/1** |
| (a) | "they protect against disease and fight infection" | **0/1** |
| (b) "State the function of the platelets." | "blood clotting and scab formation" — **the words of DA-B2-2.2.1** | **0/1** |
| (b) | "they cause clotting and form a scab" | **0/1** |

Feedback in every case: "Listing rule: more answers were given than asked for, so 1 mark is lost."
Neither stem asks for a fixed number of things, so the listing rule has nothing to police.

**Fix** — `"listingRule": false` on `.questions[0].parts[0].answer` and `.parts[1].answer`. Verified:
all four responses above 1/1, `accepted` and the scheme accepts ("fights infection", "form a scab")
1/1, "they carry oxygen" still 0/1. **Leave part (c) at `true`** — there the rule is doing its job
("Name **one** substance…": "urea and hormones" correctly scores 0/1).

### B4 [major] `q…0010` part `a` (2 marks): the expected answer, typed with its own unit, scores 0 of 2

Spec: `{"value":12,"tolerance":{"type":"dp","places":1},"unit":"%","acceptForms":["decimal","percent"]}`;
stem ends "Give your answer to one decimal place."

| typed | marks |
|---|---|
| `12` | 2/2 |
| `12.0`, `12.0%` | 2/2 |
| `12%` | **0/2** — "Give the answer to 1 decimal place: 12.0." |
| `12 %` | **0/2** — same |

`expectedDisplay` puts **"12 %"** on the feedback card as the expected answer, and typing exactly
that is marked wrong. Cause (already diagnosed in `b2-a-1.md` X1): for a percent-form answer
`parsed.value` is 0.12 while `target.value` is 12, so `checkAccuracy`'s `nearlyEqual` test fails and
the "fewer d.p. than asked but still the right value" escape never fires.

**This is the same claim as `b2-a-1.md` X1, which was recorded as not reproducing — it does
reproduce, and the discriminator is the authored value.** It bites only when the value has fewer
decimal places than the stem instructs. `q…heart.0008` (`value: 7.1`, same tolerance, same stem
wording) is unaffected: `7.1`, `7.1%` and `7.1 %` all score 3/3. The two parts that trip it are this
one and `q…heart.0010(b)` (H5), where the true answers are the exact integers 12 and 125.

**Fix (bundle side, no engine change)** — the 1 d.p. instruction buys nothing on an answer that is
exactly 12, and it is what switches the written-form demand on. Drop the sentence from the stem and
set an absolute tolerance:

- stem → `"A runner's red blood cell count rose from 5.0 million per mm³ to 5.6 million per mm³ after a month training at altitude. Calculate the percentage increase."`
- `tolerance` → `{"type":"absolute","value":0.05}`

Verified: `12`, `12%`, `12 %`, `12.0`, `12.0%` all 2/2, and the `sci.quant.percentage-wrong-denominator`
common error (10.7) still matches and still pays 1. If the trailing zero is wanted on the page,
the alternative is to keep the stem and fix `checkAccuracy`/`droppedZerosNote` to compare the
unit-reconciled value — the engine fix `b2-a-1.md` proposed.

### B5 [moderate] `q…0012` part `b` (2 marks): a statement that is false about both vessels earns 1 of 2

```json
{"any":["thinner","thin","less muscle","less elastic"],"marks":1}
```

Group 2 is vein-keyed ("it has valves", "veins have valves", …) but group 1 is not, so:

| response | marks |
|---|---|
| "The **artery** wall is thinner than the vein's, and the **artery** has valves." | **1/2** |
| "The vein wall is thicker, and the artery has valves." | 0/2 (correct) |

**Fix** — key group 1 to the vein:

```json
{"any":["vein wall is thinner","veins have a thinner wall","vein has a thinner wall","vein has a thin wall",
        "veins have thinner walls","veins have thin walls","thinner wall than an artery","thinner than the artery",
        "less muscle","less elastic","fewer elastic"],"marks":1}
```

Verified: `accepted`, `workedSolution` and two paraphrases 2/2; both swapped answers 0/2.

### B6 [moderate] `q…0012` part `c` (3 marks): only the comparative phrasing of the diffusion distance is matched

```json
{"any":["short distance","short diffusion","diffuse quickly","shorter"],"marks":1}
```

"The wall is a single cell thick, which makes the **diffusion distance short**, and it is permeable so
materials pass through." → **2/3**, "still missing short distance". The same idea written as
"the diffusion distance is short**er**" scores 3/3, so the mark turns on a comparative suffix.

**Fix** — `{"any":["short distance","short diffusion","diffuse quickly","shorter","distance is short","diffusion distance"],"marks":1}`.
Verified: that paraphrase and the "shorter" one both 3/3; "It has a thick wall to withstand high
pressure." still 0/3.

### B7 [moderate] `q…0013` part `main` (6 marks): the text-long common error fires on Band A answers, names a misconception it does not detect, and states a count it never computes

```json
{"misconception":"sci.vessels.lumen-and-wall-swapped",
 "pattern":{"kind":"text","regex":"^(?![\\s\\S]*(permeable|one cell thick))[\\s\\S]*$"},
 "feedback":"The capillary has been left out, or described without the two points that matter: a wall one cell thick, and a permeable wall. Two of the seven indicative points are there.",
 "marksTypicallyEarned":4}
```

`mark.ts` applies a `text-long` common error **unconditionally**, not only on a miss, so it lands on
good answers. Verified on the current spec:

- "An artery has a thick muscular wall for high pressure and a small lumen. A vein has a thin wall, a large lumen and valves that stop backflow. **A capillary wall is a single cell in thickness and lets materials pass through to the tissues.**" → floor **5/6 (Band A)**, and still tagged `sci.vessels.lumen-and-wall-swapped` with "The capillary has been left out".
- "…The capillary is only **a cell thick**, and **porous**, so materials are **exchanged** with the tissues." → same.

Three separate defects: the pattern detects an *absence of two spellings*, not a lumen/wall swap; the
misconception id is not the one the feedback describes; and "Two of the seven indicative points are
there" is a fixed sentence that the engine's own evidence line will usually contradict (it prints the
real count next to it). `marksTypicallyEarned: 4` is also inconsistent with its own feedback — two
indicative points is Band C, 1–2 marks — though for `text-long` the value is inert (the floor comes
from the QWC evidence).

**Fix** — broaden the lookahead, point the id at the misconception the feedback actually names, and
drop the fabricated count:

```json
{"misconception":"sci.vessels.capillary-role-unknown",
 "pattern":{"kind":"text","regex":"^(?![\\s\\S]*(permeable|porous|one cell thick|single cell|a cell thick|cell thick|exchange))[\\s\\S]*$"},
 "feedback":"The capillary is the vessel most answers thin out. Two things earn its marks: a wall one cell thick, and a permeable wall that lets materials be exchanged with the tissues.",
 "marksTypicallyEarned":2}
```

Verified: it no longer fires on either Band A answer above, and it still fires on an answer that
describes only the artery and the vein.

The note's annotated teaching diagrams are attached unchanged to the questions, so the mark scheme is
printed beside the stem. Reusing a note figure is the pack-wide pattern and is not itself the
problem; these are the cases where the figure's own text *is* the answer:

|---|---|---|
| `q…0001` | a, b, c (3 marks) | "white blood cell: it has a nucleus, **and defends the body against disease**"; "platelet: a cell fragment. **It turns fibrinogen into fibrin, so the blood clots and a scab forms**"; "plasma … **carrying cells, food molecules, carbon dioxide, hormones and urea**" |
| `q…0002` | main (3 marks) | "red blood cell: **a biconcave disc** … **with no nucleus** and **full of haemoglobin, which contains iron**" |
| `q…0003` | a, b, c (3 marks) | "**ARTERY** … carries blood away from the heart at high pressure"; "**VEIN** … carries blood back to the heart at low pressure; has valves"; "**CAPILLARY** wall one cell thick and permeable … lets materials be exchanged with the tissues" |
| `q…0008` | main (3 marks) | footnote: "**Veins carry blood at low pressure** … the valves **stop the blood sliding backwards** … **Arteries have no valves: the heart supplies the pressure**" |
| `q…0009` | main (3 marks) | "a red blood cell **has no wall** to protect it"; "**water enters by osmosis, so the cell swells**"; "**it bursts: lysis**" |

| `q…0012` | a, b, c (6 marks) | as `q…0003` |
| `q…0013` | main (6 marks) | as `q…0003` — every indicative point |

That is 31 of the bundle's marks readable off the stimulus. Same class as `b2-a-1.md` F2/F10/G5/G6.

**Fix** — give the questions a stripped copy of each figure (same geometry, leader lines and letters,
no names and no explanatory annotation) and keep the annotated version in the note. `q…0004` and
`q…0007` are fine as they are: their tables carry only the data the stem restates.

## 2. `packs/science/content/b2/b2-heart-double-circulation/bundle.json`

### H1 [major] `q…0011` part `d` (2 marks): the new reject zeroes correct paraphrases, and the swap still scores 2/2 when written with bare letters

Current (identical `reject` on both groups):

```json
"reject":["chamber c pumps","c pumps blood to the whole body","chamber d pumps only",
          "d pumps only as far as the lungs","chamber d pumps blood to the lungs"]
```

`"chamber c pumps"` is a phrase the **correct** answer has to contain — the item's own `accepted`
string is "chamber D pumps blood all the way round the body, while **chamber C pumps** only to the
lungs…", which survives only because an exact `accepted` match short-circuits the marker. Any
paraphrase does not:

| response | marks |
|---|---|
| "Chamber D pumps blood all the way round the body, but **chamber C pumps** only as far as the lungs." | **0/2** — fully correct |
| "Chamber D has to pump blood to the whole body; **chamber C pumps** just to the lungs." | **0/2** — fully correct |
| "**C** pumps to the whole body and **D** only to the lungs." | **2/2** — fully swapped |

**Fix** — key each group to its letter (and to the ventricle name, for the worked solution's wording)
and delete both `reject` lists:

```json
"keyWords": [
  {"any":["d pumps blood all the way round the body","d pumps blood round the whole body","d pumps blood round the body",
          "d pumps blood to the whole body","d pumps to the whole body","d pumps round the whole body",
          "d has to pump blood all the way round the body","d has to pump blood to the whole body",
          "d has to pump blood round the body","left ventricle and it has to pump blood all the way round the body",
          "left ventricle which pumps blood all the way round the body","left ventricle pumps blood all the way round the body",
          "left ventricle has to pump blood all the way round the body","left ventricle pumps to the whole body"],"marks":1},
  {"any":["c pumps only to the lungs","c pumps only as far as the lungs","c pumps blood only as far as the lungs",
          "c pumps blood only to the lungs","c pumps just to the lungs","c only pumps to the lungs","c pumps to the lungs",
          "c pumps blood to the lungs","c only to the lungs","right ventricle which pumps blood only as far as the lungs",
          "right ventricle pumps blood only as far as the lungs","right ventricle only pumps to the lungs"],"marks":1}
]
```

(The bare-letter entries match inside "chamber D pumps…" too, because the marker matches whole-word
phrases after normalising.) Re-run: `accepted` 2/2, `workedSolution` 2/2, both paraphrases above 2/2,
"D pumps blood all the way round the body and C pumps only to the lungs." 2/2, and both swaps —
including the bare-letter one — **0/2**.

### H2 [major] `q…0004` part `main` (2 marks): three spellings of the swap still score 2/2

Current `reject` (on both groups):

```json
["right ventricle pumps blood to the whole body","right ventricle pumps to the body",
 "right ventricle pumps blood round the body","left ventricle only pumps to the lungs",
 "left ventricle pumps blood to the lungs","left ventricle pumps only as far as the lungs"]
```

| response | marks |
|---|---|
| "The **right side** pumps to the whole body and the **left side** only to the lungs." | **2/2** |
| "The **right** ventricle pumps round the whole body; the **left** ventricle **just** pumps to the lungs." | **2/2** |
| "The **right** ventricle has to pump blood to the body, and the **left** one only to the lungs, so the right needs more muscle." | **2/2** |
| "The right ventricle pumps blood all the way round the body, while the left ventricle only pumps to the lungs." | 0/2 (caught) |

**Fix** — side-keyed groups, both `reject` lists deleted:

```json
"keyWords": [
  {"any":["left ventricle pumps blood all the way round the body","left ventricle pumps blood round the whole body",
          "left ventricle pumps blood round the body","left ventricle pumps round the whole body",
          "left ventricle pumps blood to the whole body","left ventricle pumps to the whole body",
          "left ventricle pumps blood to the body","left ventricle pumps to the body","left ventricle pumps it to the body",
          "left ventricle has to pump blood all the way round the body","left ventricle has to pump blood round the body",
          "left ventricle has to pump blood to the whole body","left side pumps to the whole body",
          "left side pumps blood round the body","left side pumps to the body"],"marks":1},
  {"any":["right ventricle only pumps to the lungs","right ventricle only pumps as far as the lungs",
          "right ventricle only pumps it to the lungs","right ventricle pumps only to the lungs",
          "right ventricle pumps only as far as the lungs","right ventricle pumps blood only as far as the lungs",
          "right ventricle pumps blood only to the lungs","right ventricle just pumps to the lungs",
          "right ventricle pumps to the lungs","right ventricle pumps blood to the lungs","right side pumps to the lungs",
          "right side only to the lungs"],"marks":1}
]
```

Re-run: `accepted`, `workedSolution` and two correct paraphrases 2/2; all four swap wordings 0/2.

### H3 [major] `q…0009` part `main` (2 marks): the reject cancels the output mark on correct answers, including the item's own scheme accept

```json
{"any":["cardiac output","output"],"marks":1,
 "reject":["decreases","decrease","reduces","reduce"]}
```

Reject words take inflections, and the list is unqualified, so the mark is cancelled by the word
wherever it appears:

| response | marks |
|---|---|
| "The heart muscle gets stronger, and the resting heart rate **decreases**, so the cardiac output at rest **increases**." | **1/2** — `"decreases" cancels the mark it sits with` |
| "The heart muscle is strengthened and **more blood is pumped per minute at rest**." — the part's own `scheme[1].accept` | **1/2** — the phrase is in no `any` list |

The first is exactly what the note teaches two blocks earlier ("A stronger heart pushes more out per
beat, so it can beat more slowly"), and what the post-diagnostic's own explanation says.

Related, same part: the common error `"output[^;\\n]*(decreases|falls|lower|less)"` uses a negated
class that stops only at `;` and newline, so it reaches across a comma — it matches "the cardiac
output at rest increases, while the resting pulse rate falls". It does no harm today (a fully correct
answer returns before common errors are applied) but it will mis-diagnose any partly-correct answer
of that shape.

**Fix** — scope the reject to the output and add the scheme's accept:

```json
{"any":["cardiac output","output","more blood pumped per minute","more blood is pumped per minute","blood pumped per minute"],
 "marks":1,
 "reject":["output decreases","output decrease","output reduces","output falls","output is lower",
           "output at rest decreases","output at rest falls","output at rest is lower"]}
```

and tighten the common error to `"output[^.;,\\n]*(decreases|falls|lower|less)"`. Verified: both
responses above 2/2, `accepted` and `workedSolution` 2/2, and the genuine misconception
("cardiac output at rest decreases" / "cardiac output at rest falls") still 1/2 with its tag.

### H4 [major] `q…0012` part `c` (3 marks): "producing energy" scores 3/3 while "produce energy" scores 2/3

```json
"reject":["make energy","makes energy","making energy","create energy","creates energy",
          "produce energy","produces energy"]
```

Phrase rejects (anything containing a space) do **not** take inflections — only single words do — so
the list catches exactly the seven spellings written:

| response | marks |
|---|---|
| "Her muscles are respiring faster **to produce energy**, …" | 2/3 (intended) |
| "Her muscles are respiring faster, **producing energy**, …" | **3/3** |
| "Her muscles are respiring faster and **generating energy**, …" | **3/3** |

The part's own common error `"(make\|makes\|making\|creat[a-z]*\|produc[a-z]*) energy"` does match
"producing energy" — so the reject list and the common error disagree about the same answer, and
because the answer scores full marks the common error is never reached.

**Fix** — spell out the inflections the common error covers:

```json
"reject":["make energy","makes energy","making energy","made energy","create energy","creates energy",
          "creating energy","created energy","produce energy","produces energy","producing energy",
          "produced energy","generate energy","generates energy","generating energy"]
```

Verified: `accepted`, `workedSolution` and a correct paraphrase 3/3; all four "energy-made" wordings 2/3.

### H5 [major] `q…0010` part `b` (3 marks): "125 %" scores 0 of 3

Identical to B4 — `{"value":125,"tolerance":{"type":"dp","places":1},"unit":"%"}` with "Give your
answer to one decimal place." in the stem, and 85 ÷ 68 × 100 = exactly 125.

| typed | marks |
|---|---|
| `125` | 3/3 |
| `125.0`, `125.0%` | 3/3 |
| `125%`, `125 %` | **0/3** — "Give the answer to 1 decimal place: 125.0." |

`expectedDisplay` shows "125 %" on the feedback card.

**Fix** — stem → `"Her resting pulse rate was 68 beats per minute. Calculate the percentage increase from rest to the peak."`,
`tolerance` → `{"type":"absolute","value":0.05}`. Verified: all five forms 3/3, and both common
errors (85 → 1/3, 225 → 2/3) still match and still pay.

### H6 [moderate] `q…0013` part `main` (6 marks): the text-long common error crosses commas and fires on Band A answers

```json
{"misconception":"sci.circulation.pulmonary-vessels-swapped",
 "pattern":{"kind":"text","regex":"right ventricle[^.;\\n]*pulmonary vein"},
 "marksTypicallyEarned":3}
```

`[^.;\n]*` stops at a full stop, semicolon or newline but not at a comma, so it runs straight through
a correct clause. Verified on the current spec:

- "The right ventricle pumps the blood into the **pulmonary artery**, which carries it to the lungs, and it comes back in the **pulmonary vein** to the left atrium." → fires; floor 3/6, tagged swapped.
- "Blood goes from the right atrium to the right ventricle, out along the **pulmonary artery** to the lungs, then back in the **pulmonary vein**, into the left atrium and left ventricle, and out through the aorta." → fires; floor **5/6 (Band A)**, tagged swapped.

Because `mark.ts` applies `text-long` common errors unconditionally, a Band A answer is told it swapped
the two vessels and the misconception is recorded.

**Fix** — add the comma to the negated class: `"right ventricle[^.;,\\n]*pulmonary vein"`. Verified:
it no longer fires on either answer above, and it still fires on both genuinely swapped answers
("The right ventricle pumps blood into the pulmonary vein, which carries it to the lungs." and "The
right ventricle sends blood to the lungs in the pulmonary vein.").

### H7 [moderate] `ftm…02`: three independently wrong lines in an item that accepts one

```json
"studentWorking":[
  "The right ventricle pumps blood into the pulmonary vein.",
  "The pulmonary vein carries it to the lungs, where it picks up oxygen.",
  "It comes back in the pulmonary artery to the left atrium, and then into the left ventricle."],
"mistakeLine":1
```

`FindTheMistake` credits a tap only on `mistakeLine`, and after a second wrong tap it gives the line
away. Lines 2 and 3 are each independently false — the pulmonary vein does not carry blood to the
lungs, and the pulmonary artery does not bring it back — and neither follows from line 1 the way a
consequential arithmetic line does. The item's own `whatWentWrong` says "The two pulmonary vessels
have been **swapped**" (plural) and the `correction` rewrites all three lines, which confirms it.
Compare the other two in this batch, which are clean: `ftm…heart.01` (70 + 68 = 138 follows correctly
from the wrong equation) and `ftm…blood.01` (42 ÷ 7 = 6 follows correctly from the unconverted line).

**Fix** — make lines 2 and 3 follow from line 1 without naming a vessel again:

```json
"studentWorking":[
  "The right ventricle pumps blood into the pulmonary vein.",
  "That vessel carries it to the lungs, where it picks up oxygen.",
  "It comes back to the left atrium, and then into the left ventricle."],
"correction":[
  "The right ventricle pumps blood into the pulmonary artery.",
  "That vessel carries it to the lungs, where it picks up oxygen.",
  "It comes back in the pulmonary vein to the left atrium, and then into the left ventricle."]
```

`marksEarnedAsWritten: ["P2"]` and the feedback ("One mark of the three: the lungs and the oxygen are
right, and so is the chamber order") both still hold after the rewrite.

### H8 [moderate] The note has lost its `hero` block

Same as B8: `note.blocks.json` now opens `["h","p","h",…]` (39 blocks, no `hero`). The `lede` survives
as block `[1]`; the three "you can" lines and `minutes: 10` are gone. Restore the `hero` at index 0
and delete the duplicate `p`.

### H9 [moderate] Question figures print the answers

| item | part(s) | figure text |
|---|---|---|
| `q…0001` | a, b (2 marks) | the letters A–D are printed **on top of** "RIGHT ATRIUM", "LEFT ATRIUM", "RIGHT VENTRICLE", "LEFT VENTRICLE" |

### H10 [minor] The note's spec callout cites the wrong page

`note.blocks.json` block `[28].source`:

```
CCEA GCSE Double Award Science specification §3.2, outcomes 2.2.5 to 2.2.7 (p.25)
```

The spec JSON gives `"page": 27` for 2.2.5, 2.2.6 and 2.2.7. (Both bundles in this batch carry the
same wrong page, which looks like one string copied twice: blood is p.26, heart is p.27.)

**Fix** — `(p.27)`.

### H11 [minor] `mustMemorise` carries an equation and a term that are not on this specification, with no not-on-spec line

```json
"Cardiac output = stroke volume × heart rate"
```

"stroke volume" appears **0 times** in `data/spec/double-award-science.json`; "cardiac output"
appears once, in 2.2.6, as an outcome of training ("strengthened heart muscle and increased cardiac
output when at rest") with no equation. `topic.notOnThisSpec` names four excluded things (the cardiac
cycle in phases, conduction/ECG, tricuspid/bicuspid/semilunar, blood pressure readings) but not this.

Most of the items handle it correctly by supplying the equation in the stem (`q…0007`, `we…01`) or in
a hint (`q…0012(b)`). The one that does not is the post-diagnostic `05` ("A person's stroke volume is
70 cm³ and her heart rate is 68 beats per minute. What is her cardiac output?"), which asks for it
from memory.

**Fix** — either add "The cardiac-output equation (supplied when a question needs it)" to
`notOnThisSpec` and soften the `mustMemorise` line, or give the equation in the diagnostic stem as
the questions do. Not a marking defect; a spec-scope flag for the reviewer.

### H12 [minor] The photo caption contradicts the viewpoint rule the note has just taught

Block `[3]` figure caption, repeated inside the SVG: "**The person's right side is on your left, as it
is in every exam diagram.**" Block `[11]` photo caption: "A real sheep heart cut across the
ventricles. **The thick-walled, round one on the left of the photograph is the left ventricle**; the
thin-walled crescent is the right." — and the block's `prompt` asks the learner "Which ventricle is
which in this photograph…".

The caption is correct about the photograph (I checked the image: thick ring with a small round
cavity on the left, thin wall and crescent cavity on the right), but a learner applying the rule two
sections earlier will read it as an error, and nothing says why a specimen in a hand is not oriented
like a diagram.

**Fix** — one clause, e.g. "…is the left ventricle — a real heart in a hand is not turned the way an
exam diagram is, so the sides are the other way round here; the thin-walled crescent is the right."

### H13 [minor] Diagnostic distractors carry misconception ids that do not describe them

| probe / option | text | tagged | registry label |
|---|---|---|---|
| pre `p1` b | "a vein" (for "carries blood AWAY from the heart") | `sci.vessels.lumen-and-wall-swapped` | "Swaps the artery's and the vein's **wall thickness or lumen size**" — this is a direction error |
| post `03` d | "It contains the valves, which need thicker muscle around them" | `sci.heart.valves-pump` | "Describes a heart valve as **pumping** or pushing the blood" |
| post `06` c | "The heart grows more valves" | `sci.heart.valves-pump` | as above |
| post `06` d | "The blood carries more carbon dioxide" | `sci.exercise.output-falls-with-training` | "States that cardiac output at rest **falls** after months of training" |

**Fix** — drop `misconception` from these four (it is optional on `McqOption`) rather than record one
the learner does not hold. The rest of the bundle's tags fit their labels exactly — `pre p1 d`
→ `artery-defined-by-oxygen`, `pre p2 b/c/d` → `valves-pump` / `valve-function-unknown`, and every
post-diagnostic swap tag are all well chosen.

## 3. Areas checked and clean

**Numbers — every one recomputed in node, all correct.** Blood: 6.0 − 2 × 1.5 = 3.0 mm lumen and the
table's vein row 6.0 − 2 × 0.5 = 5.0; the capillary twin 0.008 − 2 × 0.001 = 0.006 mm; 42 mm = 42 000
µm and 42 000 ÷ 7 = ×6000, twin 21 000 ÷ 7 = 3000 (matching note gate `g4`); 240 ÷ 3 = 80; 55 % of
5.0 dm³ = 2.75; (5.6 − 5.0) ÷ 5.0 × 100 = 12.0. Heart: 70 × 68 = 4760; 85 × 60 = 5100 (the table's
filled cell); (5100 − 4760) ÷ 4760 × 100 = 7.14 → 7.1; 110 × 153 = 16 830 (matching gate `g4`);
(153 − 68) ÷ 68 × 100 = 125.0 (matching the note's "an increase of 125.0 %"); 11 − 6 = 5 minutes.

**Every `commonError` value matches the error it describes, and every tolerance covers both the exact
and the rounded form.** 6.0 − 1.5 = 4.5 (wall once); 42 ÷ 7 = 6 (not converted); 7 ÷ 42 000 =
0.0001667 vs the authored 0.000167 ± 0.000005; 3 ÷ 240 = 0.0125; 45 % of 5.0 = 2.25; 0.6 ÷ 5.6 × 100 =
10.714 vs 10.7 ± 0.05; 70 + 68 = 138; 70 ÷ 68 = 1.029 vs 1.03 ± 0.005; 340 ÷ 5100 × 100 = 6.667 vs
6.7 ± 0.05; 153 − 68 = 85; 153 ÷ 68 × 100 = 225; 110 + 153 = 263; the end-time 11. Each one also fires
on its own value through `markAnswer` and pays exactly its `marksTypicallyEarned`.

**Figures.** The vessel cross-sections are drawn to the scale they claim: outer r = 78 px for both at
6.0 mm across (26 px/mm), artery lumen r = 39 → 3.0 mm with a 1.5 mm wall, vein lumen r = 65 → 5.0 mm
with a 0.5 mm wall — exactly the table. The spun-blood tube is 137.5 px plasma over 250 px = 55 % and
112.5 = 45 %, matching the labels and `q…0007`. The artery is drawn leftmost, so `q…0012(a)`'s "the
vessel drawn on the left" is right. The pulse graph is verified above.

**Left/right and oxygenated/deoxygenated are consistent throughout.** In both heart SVGs the right
atrium and right ventricle sit at x = 322/330 and the left pair at x = 452/478 on a 900-wide canvas
whose heart spans 250–590, so the person's right really is on the viewer's left, as the caption says;
the vena cava and pulmonary artery are labelled on the left, the aorta and pulmonary vein on the
right, "thin wall" on the right ventricle and "thick muscular wall" on the left. The double-circulation
diagram agrees (right pair x = 368, left pair x = 492, shaded box x = 430–554). The pulmonary artery
is consistently deoxygenated-away and the pulmonary vein oxygenated-towards, in the note, the `why`
callout, both diagnostics, `q…0002`, `q…0011(b)`, the order item, the retrieval prompts and the
find-the-mistake.

**Spec fit.** Blood covers 2.2.1 / 2.2.2 / 2.2.3 / 2.2.4 and heart covers 2.2.5 / 2.2.6 / 2.2.7,
matching `topic.statementIds` exactly. Cell lysis is Higher in the spec (`"tier": "H"` on 2.2.2) and
is flagged Higher in the note heading, the `mustknow`, the spec callout, the diagnostic stem and on
`q…0009` (`tier: "H"`). Platelets are given in the spec's own words (fibrinogen → fibrin, clotting,
scab formation); plasma's list is the spec's five; "haemoglobin containing iron" and the biconcave
shape are the spec's; the exercise outcome is quoted verbatim ("strengthened heart muscle and
increased cardiac output when at rest"); the four chambers, valves, wall thickness and coronary
vessels are 2.2.7. `notOnThisSpec` correctly excludes blood groups, the clotting cascade, lymph,
arterioles/venules and named wall layers (blood) and the cardiac cycle, conduction/ECG, valve names
and blood-pressure readings (heart) — so the cardiac cycle is properly out of scope, and the only
over-reach is H11. `topic.tier: "F"` on the heart bundle with two `tier: "H"` questions is the pack
convention (nine other bundles do the same, including shipped ones), not a defect.

**Multiple choice.** All 18 diagnostic probes have exactly one correct option, four options, no
duplicate texts and feedback on every option; the distractors are all genuinely wrong (the closest
call, post `05`'s "70 cm³ per minute", is wrong for the reason its feedback gives). No `mcq` answer
specs inside questions. All 12 note gates are well formed: every choice gate's answer is among its
options, and the blank gate "backwards | back | backward" uses the supported alternative form.

**Find the mistake.** `ftm…blood.01` is sound — line 2 is the only independently wrong line (line 3's
arithmetic is correct given line 2), the correction fixes it, and `fixMatches` accepts the corrected
line. `ftm…heart.01` is sound — the wrong equation is line 1, lines 2 and 3 follow it correctly, and
`marksEarnedAsWritten: []` matches "a wrong equation earns nothing". Only `ftm…heart.02` fails the
one-wrong-line contract (H7). One note on `ftm…blood.01` for the reviewer, not counted as a finding:
`marksEarnedAsWritten: ["P1"]` is the *equation* mark the feedback describes, but P1 in the linked
`q…0005` scheme and in `we…02` is the unit conversion — the mark the student did not earn. The chip
carries no scheme text, so it reads as "process mark 1"; worth a glance only.

**Order item.** `q…0003` marks correctly: the right arrangement scores 3/3, and both authored common
errors fire against the arranged item texts and pay 1 as declared (pulmonary vessels swapped, sides
reversed).

**Delimiters, placeholders, SVG integrity.** No `${`, no literal `undefined` or `NaN`, no maths
`$…$` delimiters anywhere in either bundle or note; the only `$` characters are regex end anchors,
each correctly single. No stray path data: `scripts/qa/svg-draws.mjs` reports 0 defects across 1124
SVGs, and both bundles are clean under an independent scan for path commands sitting as element text.
Both referenced photos exist with their credits (`/img/science/b2/b2-blood-and-vessels-1.jpg`, public
domain; `/img/science/b2/b2-heart-double-circulation-1.jpg`, CC BY-SA 4.0).

**Text marking, self-consistency.** Every `accepted` string and every `workedSolution` in both bundles
earns full marks, and the authoring lint (`lintKeyWords`) reports 0 hard and 0 soft findings on both.
Every misconception id used is in the registry (289 ids across science, all registered). Both
text-long worked solutions reach Band A on the QWC evidence engine (heart 7 of 7 points; blood 6 of 7,
see B10).

**Regex common errors.** No greedy `.*`, no `\bA\b` under the case-insensitive flag, and no pattern
without boundaries that matches its own correct answer — checked by running every text pattern against
that part's `accepted` strings and `workedSolution`. The two that reach across a clause are named in
H3 and H6; `q…0011(d)`'s `"^(?![\s\S]*lung)[\s\S]*$"` is an absence pattern but its misconception
(`no-comparative-language`, "only one side of the comparison is there") is what absence actually means
there, so it stands.

## Verdicts

- **`b2-blood-and-vessels`** — hold. The science, the spec fit, every number and every figure are
  correct, and `q…0009`'s regeneration is the only content change that made things worse. But two
  multi-mark text parts still pay for a reversed answer or zero a right one (B1, B2), the
  specification's own wording for platelets scores 0 on a one-mark part (B3), the expected answer
  typed with its own `%` sign scores 0 on `q…0010(a)` (B4), and the note has lost its hero block (B8).
  B1–B4 and B8 are the blocking set; B5–B7 and B9 are quick wins once you are in the file.

- **`b2-heart-double-circulation`** — hold. The route, the vessel rule, the left/right convention and
  every calculation are sound, and the pulse-graph SVG is properly fixed. But `q…0011(d)` now scores
  0 of 2 on the most natural correct paraphrase while the bare-letter swap still scores 2 of 2 (H1),
  `q…0004`'s swap survives in three wordings (H2), `q…0009` cancels the output mark on correct
  answers including its own scheme accept (H3), "producing energy" scores full marks (H4), "125 %"
  scores none (H5), and the note has lost its hero block (H8). H1–H5 and H8 are the blocking set.

- **Cross-cutting.** The hero-block deletion hit all four B2 bundles in this wave (and the four C2
  bundles), including the two `b2-a-1.md` recorded as clean — worth checking before the next batch
  regenerates. And `b2-a-1.md`'s X1 (a whole-number percentage with a `%` sign rejected) **does**
  reproduce; it bites only when the authored value has fewer decimal places than the stem instructs,
  which is why a part answering 7.1 looks clean while 12 and 125 do not.
